Finish on the Nebbiolo: its tannin would make anything after it taste thin.

items: Nebbiolo vs last week's Guérin Pinot Noir: both pale, both high acid, but feel the tannin. That's the blind-tasting tell.
Rosé de Loire vs last week's Cuomo Rosato: direct press vs short maceration, pale salmon vs deeper colour.

lineup.sub: A crisp Alpine white, a numbered Puligny-sourced Chardonnay, a bone-dry Loire rosé and a Barolo-village Nebbiolo. The Rue de Bois at $21 is the splurge pour.

wines.concl: Good to very good. Racy acidity balanced by ripe orchard fruit and a little lees richness; clean, stony length. Less complex than last week's whites, but precise and true to place.
exam: Erbaluce di Caluso is a DOCG for three styles: dry, Spumante (traditional method) and Passito (dried grapes).
Compare with the Piedmont whites on the spec: Gavi (Cortese) and Roero Arneis. Erbaluce has the highest acid of the three.
Glacial moraine soils: sand and gravel left by retreating glaciers, warm-draining and poor.
factors: Climate
Cool continental, in the Alpine foothills near the Valle d'Aosta border. Cold nights and a big day-night swing keep acidity very high.
Soil
The vineyards sit on the glacial moraine around Ivrea: sandy, gravelly, free-draining. Gives a lean, stony texture.
Grape
Erbaluce: an ancient local white with very high natural acidity. That acidity lets it make three styles: dry, traditional-method sparkling and sweet Passito.
Winemaking
La Torrazza is fermented and aged in stainless steel, with about 8 months on the lees before bottling. No oak. The lees add a little texture without hiding the fruit.
Producer
Ferrando is the leading name in the Canavese and also makes Carema, the Alpine Nebbiolo grown on stone terraces below Mont Blanc.
wines.flag: Which Ferrando Erbaluce? The front label names no cuvée. Ferrando's core estate bottling is La Torrazza (4 ha in Borgomasino, steel-fermented, about 8 months on lees); the Etichetta Verde comes from the Cariola cru. The notes below follow La Torrazza. Check the back label.
wines.name: Ferrando Erbaluce di Caluso 2025
pair: Soft goat or cow's milk cheese
wines.say: An Alpine-foothill white from northern Piedmont: crisp green apple, white flowers and wet stone. Think Gavi with more snap.
wines.sub: Erbaluce di Caluso DOCG · Canavese, northern Piedmont, Italy

wines.concl: Very good. Concentrated old-vine fruit balanced by crisp 2024 acidity; barrel and lees add a second layer; good length for a regional wine.
exam: Burgundy regional AOCs: Bourgogne, Bourgogne Côte d'Or (since 2017), Hautes-Côtes de Nuits / de Beaune.
Puligny-Montrachet Grands Crus: Montrachet, Chevalier-, Bâtard-, Bienvenues-Bâtard-Montrachet.
White Burgundy winemaking toolkit: barrel fermentation, MLF, lees ageing and stirring.
factors: Site
Higher-altitude Puligny parcels. Higher sites ripen later and keep more acid, an advantage in recent warm vintages.
Vines
Over 50 years old: lower yields and more concentration than a typical regional white.
Vintage

2024 whites had a wet spring with mildew and poor flowering, then sun from July. Yields fell about 25–40%. The wines are cooler, finer and lower in alcohol, with clear acidity. Merchants say Alvina's 2024s pair 2017's freshness with 2021's openness.
Winemaking
Aged on its lees in used barrels, mainly from the cooper François Frères; no new oak in the debut vintage. Expect texture and subtle toast rather than vanilla.
Climate
Moderate continental Côte de Beaune: the benchmark for oak-aged, mineral Chardonnay.
wines.flag: Puligny fruit at Bourgogne level. Bourgogne Côte d'Or is a regional AOC created in 2017 for Bourgogne grown inside the Côte de Nuits and Côte de Beaune. These parcels sit in Puligny-Montrachet but outside the village appellation. Alvina is Paul Pernot's granddaughter.
wines.name: Alvina Pernot Rue de Bois 2024
wines.ready: Can drink now, but has potential for ageing (critics suggest 2026–2028 and beyond).
wines.say: Puligny-Montrachet fruit from 50-year-old vines at a Bourgogne price. Only 1,296 bottles were made.
wines.sub: Bourgogne Côte d'Or AOC · Côte de Beaune, Burgundy, France

wines.concl: Very good. Taut acidity and delicate red fruit in balance; pepper and stony notes add interest beyond simple fruit.
exam: Anjou rosés: Rosé de Loire (dry) vs Rosé d'Anjou and Cabernet d'Anjou (medium-sweet).
Direct press = palest rosé; short maceration (like last week's Cuomo) = deeper colour and more body.
Skipping MLF keeps the sharp malic acid: a deliberate choice for freshness.
factors: Climate
Cool-moderate. Atlantic influence reaches up the Loire, but Anjou is relatively dry and sheltered. Fruit ripens fully while keeping acidity.
Soil
Shallow grey schist and volcanic rhyolite with a little clay, in some spots only 10–15 cm of topsoil over rock. This is 'Anjou Noir', the dark-rock side of Anjou.
Grape
Cabernet Franc: red fruit, a leafy or peppery edge, high acid, light tannin. Grolleau adds juicy, low-alcohol fruit.
Winemaking
Direct press (minimal skin contact, so the colour stays pale), native yeasts, no malolactic, fermented and aged in stainless steel. Every step protects acidity and freshness.
Producer
Thibaud trained in Gevrey-Chambertin and Savennières and founded his estate in 2009. He is best known for powerful, racy Savennières Chenin Blanc, and brings the same precision here.
wines.flag: Rosé de Loire is always dry. Don't confuse it with Rosé d'Anjou (medium-sweet, mostly Grolleau) or Cabernet d'Anjou (medium-sweet, the Cabernets). The blend changes by vintage, and some years are 100% Cabernet Franc, so check the back label for 2025.
wines.name: Thibaud Boudignon Rosé de Loire 2025
wines.ready: Drink now. Not intended for ageing.
wines.say: A dry Loire rosé from a Chenin master: pale, crisp, redcurrant and white pepper. Not a sweet Anjou rosé.
wines.sub: Rosé de Loire AOC · Anjou, Loire Valley, France

wines.concl: Very good. Firm but fine tannins and high acidity balanced by bright fruit; floral lift and savoury notes give complexity.
exam: Nebbiolo's paradox: pale colour, but high tannin and high acid. Pale garnet does not mean light structure.
Minimum ageing: Barolo 38 months (18 in wood), Barbaresco 26 months (9 in wood). Langhe Nebbiolo is the earlier-drinking step below both.
Verduno: northernmost Barolo commune, home of the Monvigliero cru and the local red Pelaverga.
factors: Climate
Moderate continental, with autumn fog (nebbia, likely the origin of the grape's name). Nebbiolo buds early and ripens late, so it needs the best-exposed slopes.
Vintage

2024 in Piedmont 'ran on rain': a wet late spring and summer with heavy disease pressure, no drought, and Nebbiolo picked in October under autumn rain. Lower sugar than 2023 and good acidity: expect fresh, elegant wines with moderate alcohol.
Grape
Nebbiolo: thin skins, so pale colour, but high acid and high tannin. Aromas of red cherry, rose, violet, later tar and dried herbs.
Winemaking
Recent vintages: fermented in steel with a long maceration, then 12–18 months in oak. Much less ageing than Barolo, so the fruit stays forward.
Sources
The estate farms about 10 ha in Verduno and Barbaresco. Langhe Nebbiolo usually comes from younger vines or sites outside the Barolo/Barbaresco crus.
wines.flag: The violet on the label is a tasting clue. "Viola mammole" is sweet violet, one of Nebbiolo's signature aromas. Verduno is a Barolo village, and the Burlotto family has owned the castle since 1909. In 1838 King Carlo Alberto bought it, and General Staglieno made some of the first modern dry Nebbiolos there.
wines.name: Castello di Verduno Langhe Nebbiolo 2024
wines.ready: Can drink now, but has potential for ageing (3–5 years).
wines.say: Barolo's younger sibling, from a castle in a Barolo village: pale but grippy, with rose, violet and sour cherry.
